summary: Frontend-only mobile preview review: dashboard zero state, footer, quick-action visibility, and initial payment sheet loaded. Remaining interaction flow was blocked by the action-sheet item falling outside the 375x667 viewport during tap automation.

ui_bugs.issue: On a 375x667 mobile viewport, the visible Add payment row resolved outside the viewport when tapped, preventing navigation without forced automation; verify sheet height/scrolling and safe-area layout on Android web/native.

issues: Action rows need reliable in-viewport placement or scrolling on small screens.

action_items: Verify quick-action sheet remains tappable within the Android 375x667-equivalent viewport.
Add strict calendar-date validation; dateValue currently accepts rollover dates such as 31/02.
Ensure generated PDF includes the requested category breakdown; current HTML contains summary and itemized payments only.
critical_code_review_comments: Date parsing checks day <= 31 but does not verify the constructed Date matches the entered day/month.
PDF generation builds no category-breakdown section despite the product requirement.
Several repeated breakdownLine style keys are duplicated in the style object; harmless at runtime but indicates cleanup opportunity.
seed_data_creation: No seed data created; the attempted payment flow did not persist because the mobile action-sheet tap was blocked.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Dashboard loaded at the supplied public preview URL with zero total, ₹ formatting, footer, month/week controls, category dropdown, and FAB. Quick actions were visible. Three attempts to proceed were stopped after the same mobile viewport interaction issue; do not keep changing selectors—first inspect sheet positioning/scroll behavior.
rca_of_issue: Likely bottom-sheet content is rendered below the small viewport or the native Modal/web wrapper does not scroll its content. The action text is present and visible in the DOM, but Playwright reports it outside the viewport when clicked. Reproduce on 375x667 and Android before changing business logic.
